note: Strategy on CD127 × CD69 — the tissue-specific sub-gate of this cohort. Two clusters along CD127 plus a CD69+/- split: (1) CD127 is bimodal — dense CD127+ cluster on the right, sparser CD127- cluster on the left. (2) CD69 splits each side into an upper (CD69+) band and a lower (CD69-) band. Th1_CD127p_CD69p: tissue-resident Th1 with homeostatic signaling retained (Trm-like Th1) — upper-right quadrant (CD127+, CD69+). Th1_CD127p_CD69n: non-resident / circulating memory Th1 — lower-right quadrant (CD127+, CD69-). Th1_CD127n_CD69p: tissue-resident Th1 with homeostatic receptor down-regulated — upper-left quadrant (CD127-, CD69+). Th1_CD127n_CD69n: non-resident, non-memory-maintenance Th1 — lower-left quadrant (both -). Tissue caveat: in non-lymphoid tissues CD69+ marks residency and the upper band is well populated; in blood samples (412C_Blood, 423_Pre-blood) CD69+ is sparse and reflects early activation rather than residency. Parent caveat: this Th1 compartment includes the plastic CXCR3+CCR6+ Th1/17 subset.
tips: Th1 residency / memory-maintenance state (CD127 × CD69 quadrants) — the key tissue-specific sub-gate of this cohort. Parent caveat: Step 6 'Th1' includes CXCR3+CCR6+ (Th1/17 plastic) events. CD127 (IL-7Rα) is a homeostatic / memory-maintenance receptor. CD69 in non-lymphoid tissues is widely used as a Trm marker (rather than purely early activation as in blood); together with CD103 it forms a core Trm signature, though CD69 alone is not sufficient and CD103-negative Trm populations exist (e.g. liver, airway). Th1_CD127p_CD69p: CD127+ CD69+. Th1_CD127p_CD69n: CD127+ CD69-. Th1_CD127n_CD69p: CD127- CD69+. Th1_CD127n_CD69n: CD127- CD69-. CD103 IS in panel — combining CD69+CD103+ further supports a core Trm phenotype. In Blood samples (412C_Blood, 423_Pre-blood), CD69+ should be read as early activation, not residency.
